_README: Re-shoot a clip from a new camera angle on the Apache-2.0-only Wan 2.2 path.
ComfyUI API-format workflow. Node category: Cinematographer.
This is the licence-clean alternative to reshoot_ltx_crossview.json: every model in
the critical path is Apache-2.0 or open, with no revenue-capped community licence and
no closed API. Same camera-steering engine (CrossView-Warp), different renderer.
STATUS: NOT VERIFIED. This graph has never been executed. It was authored from real
node schemas (see PROVENANCE) but no ComfyUI instance was available where it was
written, so nothing here is a claim that it runs. What IS verified is structural, and
you can re-run it yourself:  python3 workflows/validate_graphs.py
That checks the file parses as JSON, that every node has class_type + inputs, that
every class_type is in a table of output-slot counts read from the node sources, that
every link resolves to an existing node id and a slot that node declares, that the
graph is acyclic, and that every node is reachable from a SaveVideo. It does NOT check
that ComfyUI accepts the prompt. Treat the first run as a debugging session.
NAMING NOTE -- read this before filing a bug. The file is named ..._fun_control.json
because the concrete Wan 2.2 checkpoint is Fun-Control. The conditioning family is
VACE-style control-video (a control clip drives the structure of the output), which is
why earlier revisions of this file said 'vace'. ComfyUI ships no Wan 2.2 VACE
checkpoint: every video_wan_vace_* template in Comfy-Org/workflow_templates points at
wan2.1_vace_14B_fp16.safetensors, which is Wan 2.1. Wan 2.2's control-video model is
Fun-Control. To move to true VACE instead,
replace node 16 with WanVaceToVideo and add TrimVideoLatent after the sampler, and
point node 8 at wan2.1_vace_14B_fp16.safetensors; the control_video wiring is
unchanged. Both are Apache-2.0.
PROVENANCE. Derived from ComfyUI's own template:
Comfy-Org/workflow_templates  templates/video_wan2_2_14B_fun_control.json
(read 2026-10-29; UI format, converted to API format by hand)
Input names were read from the actual node sources rather than guessed:
ComfyUI master  comfy_extras/nodes_wan.py       Wan22FunControlToVideo
ComfyUI master  comfy_extras/nodes_moge.py      LoadMoGeModel, MoGeInference
ComfyUI master  comfy_extras/nodes_video.py     LoadVideo, GetVideoComponents,
CreateVideo, SaveVideo
ComfyUI master  comfy_extras/nodes_images.py    ImageScale, ImageFromBatch
ComfyUI master  nodes.py                        UNETLoader, CLIPLoader, VAELoader,
CLIPTextEncode, ModelSamplingSD3,
KSamplerAdvanced, VAEDecode
Cseti           ComfyUI-CrossViewWarp/crossview_warp_node.py   CrossViewWarp
DELIBERATE DELTAS from that template, and only these:
1. The Canny control preprocessor is replaced by CrossViewWarp. That is the whole
point of the entry: a geometry-steered control clip (the source reprojected into
the requested camera pose, magenta where the source never saw) instead of edges.
2. ref_image is wired to frame 0 of the source clip through ImageFromBatch, instead
of the template's separate LoadImage. The identity anchor is the clip you are
re-shooting, not a second file to keep in sync.
3. The template's muted second branch (the 1.3B VACE model, mode 4) is dropped, as an
API export drops muted nodes.
4. The lightx2v 4-step LoRAs are deliberately NOT used. They are a throughput hack
that changes what the graph does; this graph is about geometry, not speed. The
template's own 20 steps / cfg 3.5 two-stage high-noise -> low-noise sampler is
kept as-is.
5. WanCameraEmbedding's 9 camera presets are deliberately NOT used. The entry's
argument is a computed judgement, not a preset: the camera comes from
CrossViewWarp, driven by the same pose the Cinematographer nodes grade.
6. filename_prefix -> cinematographer/*, to namespace the outputs.
7. The positive prompt is an obvious placeholder. If a generated clip ever shows
PLACEHOLDER_POSITIVE_PROMPT_INJECTION_DID_NOT_RUN, injection did not run; that is
the signal it is there for.
8. LoadVideo.file is a placeholder filename. The app overwrites it with the uploaded
clip on every request.
9. roll_lock / frame_count / interpolation are passed explicitly on CrossViewWarp.
The node keeps those widget slots (hidden and ignored) because ComfyUI stores
widget values positionally; passing them by name is harmless and keeps the file
diffable against a future re-export.
10. The negative prompt is Wan's own recommended negative, verbatim -- the same string
the upstream Wan 2.2 examples carry.
WHAT IS VERIFIED vs NOT:
VERIFIED      valid JSON; class_type + inputs on every node; every link resolves to
an existing node id and a declared output slot; acyclic.
NOT VERIFIED  that ComfyUI accepts this prompt; that the node packs and weights below
are installed; that it produces a clip; that the clip matches the
requested angle. None of that has been run.
REQUIRED NODE PACKS (custom):
ComfyUI-CrossViewWarp   (Apache-2.0)   CrossViewWarp
Everything else is ComfyUI core.
REQUIRED WEIGHTS (paths as ComfyUI names them):
models/diffusion_models/wan2.2_fun_control_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
models/diffusion_models/wan2.2_fun_control_low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors
models/text_encoders/umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors
models/vae/wan_2.1_vae.safetensors
models/geometry_estimation/moge_2_vitl_normal_fp16.safetensors
LICENCE. Wan 2.2 weights are Apache-2.0; CrossView-Warp and its node pack are
Apache-2.0; MoGe-2 is open. No MiniMax H3, no closed API, no revenue-capped licence
anywhere in the critical path. This is the zero-caveat stack.
MEASURED: nothing. No timing, no VRAM figure, no output. The reference app this is
modelled on was demonstrated on a 96 GB GPU; Wan 2.2 Fun-Control 14B fp8 is lighter,
but that is an expectation, not a measurement.
